driver: The decisive quantity is the time a unit takes to pass through a fixed sequence of stages whose durations are recorded for each stage in each short period of the day, while the delay at the later stages builds during the unit's own passage; the unit reaches each later stage later, so each stage has to be read at the period the unit enters it, and adding every stage at the period the unit sets off reads the later stages before their delay has built, puts the passage too short and the latest start too late.
driver_concrete: The shuttle's trip from the remote lot to the campus is built from the probe travel times on sixteen segments, recorded for vehicles entering each segment in each five-minute period; the morning queue at the I-264 merge grows while the shuttle is on its way, so only reading each segment at the five-minute period the shuttle reaches it (the trip as a vehicle experiences it) puts the latest departure at 7:05 a.m., while adding every segment for the period of departure (the instantaneous corridor time) puts it at 7:15.
stump: A competent solver takes the route's segments in order, adds the fixed access legs, uses the passenger-vehicle travel times and, for each evidence weekday and each slot, adds up the segments' travel times for the five-minute period the shuttle leaves in, filing 7:15 a.m. (on time on 235 of 250 weekdays, 94.0 per cent) against 7:05; the step that lands it there is reading every segment at the moment of departure, when the shuttle reaches the I-264 queue twenty to thirty minutes later, after it has grown, so the trip it adds up is one no vehicle made, and a 7:15 departure would have reached the stop by 8:00 on only 156 of those weekdays (62.4 per cent).
analyst_test: An analyst who reads the probe export, the segment table, the route definition and the evidence calendar correctly (the passenger class, the segments in order, the access legs, weekdays other than the observed holidays) and computes each day's trip time as the sum of the segments' travel times for the departure's five-minute period files 7:15 a.m.; the reflexes on top of it (dropping incident days as non-recurrent, a reading at the trip's midpoint, the 90th-percentile time-of-day profile walked or read at departure) file 7:15, 7:10, 7:00 or 7:10, never the 7:05 that only reading each segment at the moment the shuttle reaches it gives.
domain_test: The call turns on experienced trip-time reliability, transport network analysis that composes a vehicle's journey from segment travel times read at the moment the vehicle reaches each segment as the morning queue builds, and sets a timetable departure from the share of days it arrives on time; with another field's nouns there is no probe segment, no epoch a vehicle enters, no queue spilling back through the segments ahead of it, and the task stops reading the same.
layer1: a probe vendor's TMC travel-time export split by month, three vehicle classes (all, passenger, freight) in one file, a data-density flag, epochs in local time across both daylight-saving changes, speed and reference-speed columns beside travel time, and missing epochs at night on the arterial segments

a TMC identification table with road order, miles, direction and the network vintage, where the route joins and leaves the freeway part-way along two segments, so the route definition carries fixed access legs

the operator's 2027 proposal as a PDF: hourly platform rate, a minimum paid block, an early-start differential tied to the driver's report time, and an estimated deadhead schedule computed before the operator moved its garage
the operator's vehicle GPS export for the hospital's existing shuttle and three August 2026 route-survey runs, timestamps in UTC, pull-out and pull-in events with coordinates
an HR extract whose home postal code is the payroll mailing address (a post-office box for some rural staff), scheduled start held as an integer HHMM, effective-dated rows
a parking reassignment list keyed by employee number, a later opt-out file, and a separate permit registry carrying each vehicle's garaging ZIP

lineage.fate: spent at stage 2: the precise estimand names the overlay, no stump power (any precise statement of acres burned on state-protected land sends the solver to overlay every perimeter, a single join over section-tabulated footprints, so only Layer 1 hygiene stood between the strongest solver and the golden)
lineage.niche: a state fire agency's planning bands for staging contracted air tankers and extended-attack crews: the fire sizes above which fires carry 50, 80 and 95 per cent of the acres burned on state-protected land in 2011 to 2025, built from incident records, final perimeters and an effective-dated responsibility-area map
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a weighted cut of a size distribution whose weights are each event's footprint inside a zone rather than the whole event attributed to the zone of its starting point, so every event's area has to be apportioned across zones by overlaying its final extent on the zone map in force; attributing whole events to their point of origin drops the largest events that start outside and run in, and puts every cut too low.
lineage.stump: A competent solver merges the mutual-aid duplicates on the national incident number, retypes escaped prescribed burns from their conversion events, ranks fires by final size and accumulates acres to 50, 80 and 95 per cent, attributing each fire's whole final size to the responsibility area of its origin point as the incident table records it, and files an 80 per cent boundary near 1,680 acres against about 2,690; the step that lands them there is point-of-origin attribution of an areal event, when the plan protects the acres burned on state land and the largest fires that burn it start on federal ground.

lineage.fate: spent at stage 2 under main's literal-determinism rule (2026-10-11): the RMP annex as shipped executed word for word to the cut of the reactions on file (ILD month 16), so 16 against 20 was a reading of the population term (a fork); filed outright to include reactions not yet begun, every natural truncation-aware construction (cohorts from 480 days, the 2023 starters, reweighting, the reverse-time product-limit) filed the golden month 20, so no stump was left; the ask layer also failed the cracker sheet (pair ceiling 70.1)
lineage.niche: a specialty pharmaceutical company's drug safety department setting, in the risk management plan update filed with its next periodic safety update report, the routine monitoring window for each identified risk of an oral immunomodulator launched in April 2023: the month of treatment by which 80 and 95 per cent of that risk's reactions have begun, estimated from the post-marketing cases in the safety database at the data lock
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a cut of a time-to-event distribution observed only through events that have already happened by a fixed lock date, among units whose start dates crowd toward the lock because uptake keeps rising, so every observed event carries its own truncation time (the lock minus its start) and the distribution has to be estimated with risk sets bounded by those times; reading the cut straight off the observed events under-represents long times, because most units started too recently to reach them, and puts every long-tailed cut too low.
lineage.stump: A competent solver keeps the version of each case current at the lock, merges duplicate reports through the register, maps reactions to risks with the RMP term list, computes every reaction's time to onset from the first dose of its course wherever both dates are complete, and reads the 80 and 95 per cent months per risk straight off the reported reactions, filing the ILD window at month 16 against month 20; the step that lands them there is treating the reported times to onset as the distribution of onset, when over half of all patients started in the twelve months before the lock and their later reactions have not begun yet, so the series under-represents exactly the onsets that set the 95 per cent cut.
